comment: The Documentation page's contents (docs.js) - in c³ and on the website (make site). A group lists guides (the reader's order: previous / next follow it) (id: www/docs/<id>.html, written for the reader from the Markdown in 'from') and repositories (repo: opens it on GitHub). 'from' is where a guide's facts come from, 'at' the commit of that repository it was last brought up to date with - tools/docsStale.py lists the guides whose sources changed since. 'privateGroup': the private repositories of that kind the user can read are added to it, in c³ only (GET /api/repos/private).

items.about: The small things every library of the stack needs and none should write again: strings, files, time, the CPU count and the memory limit, daemonizing, checksums, the error stack, coroutines (corCo) and parking a coroutine in an event loop (corCoLoop) - and the library log macros (COR_LIB_*), through which a library logs without depending on corLog.
items.title: corBase API
items.desc: basic utilities - every header, generated

items.about: The log of every program of the stack. Lines are classed (F T V I W E X), and traces are numbered: each library owns a range of trace levels, switched on with --traceLevels or /admin/log while the broker runs. The level is tested inline, so a trace that is off costs a load and a branch and its arguments are never evaluated; a release build compiles the traces out.
items.title: corLog API
items.desc: logging and trace levels - every header, generated

items.about: Memory for work that ends all at once - a request, a parse, a notification: an arena hands out zeroed, aligned pieces of a buffer by moving a pointer, and a reset gives all of it back in one go. No free per object, no leak of a forgotten one. Every request of the broker has its arena.
items.title: corAlloc API
items.desc: request arenas - every header, generated

items.about: The command line of every program of the stack, from one table: each option's name, short name, type, range, default, environment variable and help. corArgs parses the command line and the environment against it, refuses a value of the wrong type or out of range, and prints -u / -U from the same table - so the help cannot disagree with what is accepted.
items.title: corArgs API
items.desc: command-line options and environment variables - every header, generated

items.about: Hash tables for the stack: chained, with the hash and compare functions the caller supplies, their items allocated from a corAlloc arena.
items.title: corHash API
items.desc: hash tables - every header, generated

items.about: One shape for data, all through the stack. A request body is parsed into a tree of CorNodes; the NGSI-LD library checks, expands and renders that same tree; a database plugin is handed trees to store and hands trees back from every read - what it keeps them as is its own business (corDB keeps the trees themselves, MongoDB gets BSON); the response is rendered from a tree, and cor:// sends a tree to another broker in binary (corTreeBin) without ever turning it into JSON text. No layer converts data for the next one, which makes corTree the API every plugin - a database plugin above all - is written against. The library builds, navigates, edits, clones and sorts trees, and keeps the ones that outlive a request in the tree heap. A node is 40 bytes, a scalar node 32; four of those bytes (flags, kind, termId) belong to the code that uses the tree, for what it knows about a node - an attribute's type, a core term - so that it need not keep it beside the tree.
items.title: corTree API
items.desc: the CorNode tree - every header, generated

items.about: JSON text into a corTree, and a corTree back out as JSON - compact or indented. The parser is the way every JSON body enters the broker; the renderers are the way every JSON response leaves it. With it comes corJson, the command-line tool.
items.title: corJson API
items.desc: the JSON parser and renderers - every header, generated

items.about: JSON-LD as NGSI-LD needs it: @context documents parsed, downloaded and cached; the terms of a corTree expanded to IRIs by a context and compacted back; the core context and its vocabulary.
items.title: corJsonld API
items.desc: JSON-LD @context handling - every header, generated

items.about: NGSI-LD semantics, on corTrees: payloads checked and attribute types detected, the core terms as an enum, the representations rendered (normalized, concise, simplified), q, geoQ and scopeQ, the subscription and registration caches, notifications, distributed operations. The broker's NGSI-LD behaviour lives here; the broker itself wires it to an HTTP server and a store.
items.title: corNgsild API
items.desc: NGSI-LD semantics - every header, generated

items.about: The NGSI-LD store inside the broker, as a database plugin: corDB.so keeps the current state in memory as corTrees - persistent on disk with --dbDir - with its own history (--troe corDB) and Timepoint; ramDB.so is the same store in memory only. No database server.
items.title: corDB API
items.desc: the in-process store - every header, generated

items.about: Prometheus metrics: counters, gauges and histograms, updated with atomics on the hot path and rendered in the Prometheus text format only when they are scraped.
items.title: corProm API
items.desc: Prometheus metrics - every header, generated

items.about: The plugin loader: a plugin named on the command line is resolved to a shared library in the plugin directory, loaded, and its registration function called - and a plugin built for another CorNode layout is refused instead of reading every node at the wrong offsets.
items.title: corPlugin API
items.desc: the plugin loader - every header, generated

items.about: An HTTP/1.1 server and nothing else: a request is parsed in place in its connection's read buffer - nothing copied - and handed to one callback with its method, path, query, headers and body. It is coraine's built-in HTTP server (COR_HTTP_SERVER=builtin), in place of libmicrohttpd.
items.title: corHttp API
items.desc: the built-in HTTP server - every header, generated

items.about: The REST layer between the HTTP server and the broker's services: a service table that routes each request to its service routine, the per-request state, the worker pools - and the clients the broker sends with - its own HTTP client, on sockets and OpenSSL, and the cor:// client - for notifications and distributed operations.
items.title: corRest API
items.desc: the REST layer and its clients - every header, generated

items.about: The contract a bridge plugin implements - the seam between NGSI-LD and a transport that is not NGSI-LD: the entry points the broker calls to start a bridge, hand it its Channels and write to them, and the callbacks it gives the bridge for what arrives (samples, replies, goal events).
items.title: corBridge API
items.desc: the bridge plugin contract - every header, generated
